domain_guidance.summary: This domain covers the fundamental concepts of wealth management, carefully distinguishing retail banking from wealth and private banking, while exploring client relationships and high net worth psychology for advisory professionals.

This domain examines the structure and operation of Indian and global financial systems, corporate finance principles, capital markets, and debt versus equity instruments utilized by modern financial practitioners across various market environments.

This domain focuses on investment vehicles used in wealth management, protection versus accumulation, mutual funds, unit trusts, bonds, Sukuk instruments, and structured savings plans designed specifically for diverse investors.

This domain addresses the calculation and evaluation of investment risk and returns within wealth management portfolios and financial planning frameworks to ensure proper asset allocation and effective client goal alignment.

This domain explores insurance concepts and risk management, including term life insurance, Takaful, annuities, and other life products utilized for wealth protection and long-term financial security planning among clients.

This domain analyzes the role of wealth management within banking operations, client retention strategies, and effective marketing of finance products to build enduring relationships with high net worth clients over time.

This domain covers legalities and regulatory frameworks relevant to wealth management practices, trusts, and family office structures to ensure full compliance with applicable laws, regulations, and industry standards.

This domain reviews tax laws applicable to wealth management, investment strategies, and asset structures to help financial advisors minimize tax liabilities for individual clients and family groups during planning.

This domain examines life cycle management principles for individual clients, asset allocation, and financial planning across different life stages to address changing capital needs over time effectively for advisors.

This domain focuses on intergenerational wealth transfer, estate planning, and tax planning strategies for managing inherited wealth and preserving family assets across multiple generations successfully in advisory practice.

This domain covers equity analysis, assessing the value of listed companies, and evaluating reported financial performance through detailed financial statement analysis and company valuation metrics for wealth portfolios.

This domain broadly explores alternative investment products within wealth management, including private equity, initial public offerings, mergers and acquisitions, hedge funds, and various commodities designed for sophisticated client portfolios everywhere.
This domain addresses real estate valuation and analysis within the context of asset classes and diversified wealth portfolios to evaluate property investments as part of holistic financial plans.

study_focus: Psychology of high net worth investors
domain_guidance.summary: This domain examines behavioural finance concepts, client psychology, and decision-making patterns of high net worth investors to better understand how emotional biases affect financial choices and advisory engagements.

This domain focuses on relationship management by a wealth manager, advanced selling techniques, lead generation, client meetings, and communication tools necessary for building long-term client trust and loyalty.

This domain covers loan and debt management strategies, credit utilization, and debt versus equity considerations in financial planning to help clients manage liabilities alongside their asset accumulation effectively.

This domain explores portfolio management strategies, modern portfolio theory, risk, diversification, model portfolios, and structured products to build structured investment solutions aligned with specific client risk tolerances.

This domain addresses international tax rules, cross-border trust planning, and global investment structures for wealth management clients who hold multi-jurisdictional assets and require professional cross-border advisory services.

This domain focuses on detailed wealth management planning, integrating financial planning concepts, diverse asset classes, and specific client requirements into a cohesive, actionable long-term financial strategy for individuals.

This domain carefully covers advanced wealth management topics, sophisticated portfolio structures, and identifying emerging market opportunities in advanced regions for high net worth investors seeking superior long-term returns.

editorial.exam_day_guidance: Arrive fully prepared for the 180-minute examination consisting of exactly 85 questions. Read each test question carefully and manage your time effectively across all twenty curriculum domains.

faq.answer_text: The examination consists of a total of 85 questions designed to test your knowledge across the twenty curriculum domains covered by AAFM India during your preparation.
faq.question_title: How many questions are on the exam?

faq.answer_text: The passing score for the examination is 50% (80/160), which corresponds to the required marks needed to successfully earn the CWM designation from AAFM India.
The exam has a duration of 180 minutes, providing candidates with three hours to complete all 85 questions within the designated testing period administered by AAFM India.
The CWM Chartered Wealth Manager certification is administered by AAFM India, which provides the official curriculum materials, guides, and testing requirements needed for professional certification.
faq.question_title: What organization certifies the CWM Chartered Wealth Manager?

editorial.meta_description: Prepare for the CWM Chartered Wealth Manager certification by reviewing curriculum domains, exam duration, passing score, and question count.
editorial.overview: The CWM Chartered Wealth Manager certification, administered by AAFM India, covers twenty distinct curriculum domains ranging from wealth management concepts to advanced portfolio strategies. It evaluates professional knowledge in financial systems, investment vehicles, insurance, legalities, tax laws, and relationship management for finance practitioners seeking professional credentialing and standard career advancement.
editorial.preparation_strategy: Review all twenty domains using official curriculum materials and guides from AAFM India to properly prepare for the certification test. Focus your study efforts on core investment products, asset allocation principles, modern portfolio theory, and international tax planning strategies. For complete guidance on certification requirements, check with AAFM India.
editorial.who_should_take: Private bankers, wealth managers, retail branch managers, corporate account managers, family office professionals, brokerage analysts, investment advisors, financial planners, investment managers, stock market professionals, and portfolio managers with financial services experience or appropriate graduate education.
